newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Fazio warns interest rate "stick" at hand.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Fazio warns interest rate "stick" at hand.

text.p: Italian central bank governor Antonio Fazio said he had cut interest rates to a 20-year low because the time was right but warned he still had a "stick" at the ready if conditions changed.

"I dropped my guard because current conditions allowed it but I'm waiting to see what happens in the next few weeks and I always have a stick firmly in my hand," La Stampa quoted him as saying on Wednesday.

The Bank of Italy announced on Tuesday night it was cutting the official discount rate to 6.75 percent from 7.50 percent and the fixed term advances, or Lombard rate, to 8.25 percent from 9.00 percent. Both cuts take effect on Wednesday.
The reduction followed preliminary inflation data from 11 Italian cities which pointed to consumer prices rising 2.6 percent year-on-year in January, unchanged from the last two months.
The rate cut, to the lowest level since September 1975, is the third in six months. Fazio had previously kept monetary policy tight and interest rates unchanged for more than a year.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi hailed the rate cut and said it would give a new impulse to development.
